καθότι
(= καθ᾽ ὅ τι), 
adv., [in LXX: Exo.1.12, 17 (אֲשֶׁר), Tob.1.12, Jdt.2.13, al. ;] 
__1. in dl., according as, just as (Ex, l.with): Act.2.45; 4.35. 
__2. In late Gk. = διότι (Tob, l.with), because: Luk.1.7; 19.9, Act.2.24; 17.31.†
(AS)

καθώς, (i.e. καθ᾽ ὡς), Hellenistic for καθά, which see, καθάπερ, καθό, καθότι (Mayser, 485; Eutherford, NPhr., 495; Bl., §78, 1), 
according as, even as, just as, as: Luk.1.2 (see: καθά), 24:39, Jhn.5.23, Act.7.48, 1Co.8.2, Gal.3.6, al.; before οὕτως, Luk.11.30, Jhn.3.14, 2Co.1.5, Col.3.13, 1Jn.2.6, al.; before καί, Jhn.15.9, 1Co.15.49, 1Jn.2.18, al.; οὕτως . . . κ., Luk.24.24 id. with ellipsis of οὕτως, Mat.21.6,…

καί, 
conj., 
and 
__I. Copulative. 
__1. Connecting single words; 
__(a) in general: Mat.2.18; 16.1, Mrk.2.15, Luk.8.15, Heb.1.1, al. mult.; repeated before each of the terms in a series, Mat.23.23, Luk.14.21, Rom.7.12; 9.4, al.
__(b) connecting numerals (WM, §37, 4): Jhn.2.20, Act.13.20; 
__(with) joining terms which are not mutually exclusive, as the part with the whole: Mat.8.33; 26.59, Mrk.16.17, Act.5.29, al. …

καινός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX (Ezk.11.19, al.) for חָדָשׁ, exc. Isa.65.15 (אַחֵר) ;] 
of that which is unused or unaccustomed, new in respect to form or quality, fresh, unused, novel: opposite to παλαιός, ἀρχαῖος, Mat.9.17; 13.52, Mrk.2.21-22 Luk.5.36, 38, 2Co.5.17, Eph.4.24; πλήρωμα, Mrk.2.21 μνημεῖον, Mat.27.60, Jhn.19.41; διαθήκη (T, WH, R, txt., omit), Luk.22.20, 1Co.11.25, 2Co.3.6, Heb.8.8" (LXX), Heb.8.13; 9.15;…

καινότης, -ητος, ἡ
(καινός), [in LXX: 3Ki.8.53, Ezk.47.12 * ;] 
__1. novelty (Thuc., Isocr., LS, see word). 
__2. freshness, newness: ἐν κ. ζωῆς (see Lft., Notes, 296), Rom.6.4 ἐν κ. πνεύματος, Rom.7.6.†
(AS)

καίπερ concessive particle, 
[in LXX: Pro.6.8, Wis.11.9, Jon.1.13, Mac.11 * ;] 
although: with ptcp., Php.3.4, Heb.5.8; 7.5; 12.17, 2Pe.1.12.†
(AS)
